html:
Wessex, the kingdom of the West Saxons, was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom in southern England from about 519 to 927. It is on the map for 800 and 900, and it became the core of England.

In 825 King Egbert beat Mercia and made Wessex the strongest English kingdom. Then the Great Heathen Army of Danes arrived in 865 and destroyed the other kingdoms one by one. Alfred the Great was nearly beaten too, but in 878 he won at Edington. He then built fortified towns, the burhs, a navy and a new army, and left the Danelaw to the Danes in the east. He had books turned into English and called himself King of the Anglo-Saxons.

His son Edward the Elder and grandson Æthelstan conquered the Danish lands. When Æthelstan took York in 927 he became the first king of all England, and Wessex merged into it. The Viking wars had made it.
sum: Wessex, the kingdom of the West Saxons, was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom in southern England from about 519 to 927. It is on the map for 800 and 900, and it became the core of England.
